To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) T cell subsets express distinct chemokine receptor repertoires, which can be modified by cytokines, 2) the expression of CCR5 can be regulated by interleukin-2, 3) the expression of chemokine receptors is associated with Th1/Th2 polarization, 4) chemokine receptors can be used as markers for Th cell subsets, 5) chemokine receptor–mediated chemotaxis can be used to identify Th
chemokine receptor programs of expression are markers of naive versus polarized T cell differentiation and that these programs are flexible and can be modulated by cytokines.
the chemokine receptors CXCR3, CCR3, and CCR4 are expressed on human T cell subsets and that their expression is regulated by cytokines and is associated with Th cell polarization.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of the chemokine system in the migration and activation of T cells, and in the development of T cell subsets.
the role of chemokine receptors in the selective recruitment of leukocytes.
the molecular basis of selective migration and the role of chemokines in this process.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
chemokines and their respective receptors play an important role in the selective migration of effector cells.
chemokine receptor genes are expressed in a flexible program, which can be modulated by cytokines, and that this program is associated with the polarization of naive T cells into functional subsets.

chemokines and chemokine receptors play a role in the recruitment of Th1 and Th1 lymphocytes into the site of inflammation, and that this recruitment is dependent on the expression of specific chemokine receptors on the Th1 and Th cells.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
chemokines and their cognate receptors are critical elements for the selective trafficking of T lymphocytes.
chemokine receptor genes can be induced in naive T cells by cytokines, and that chemokine expression can be regulated in polarized T cells by cytokine exposure.
the chemokines and chemokine receptors can be used as markers for the different types of T helper cells.
The main takeaway from our work is that
chemokine receptor programs are flexible and can be influenced by the cytokine environment.
chemokine receptor patterns are not fixed and are subject to modulation by cytokine environment.
there is a very flexible pattern of chemokine and chemokine receptor usage by different T cell subsets.
